papers.title: Stargate: Security Analysis and Mission-Aware Firewall for the CubeSat Space Protocol
papers.abstract: The CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP) is widely used for communication in CubeSat missions, yet its security model and attack surface remain largely unexplored. In this work, we present a systematic security analysis of CSP and identify fundamental limitations in its trust assumptions, coarse-grained network abstractions, privileged management services, application command semantics, and lack of mission-context awareness. Based on these findings, we develop a taxonomy of CSP attacks spanning four classes: network identity abuse, management service abuse, application semantic abuse, and mission context abuse. We then introduce Stargate, a modular, mission-aware firewall that enforces CSP-specific policies derived from this taxonomy, including node and service authorization, command-level filtering, and mission-context constraints. We implement Stargate and evaluate it on a virtual testbed based on a real-world CubeSat mission and flight software. Stargate successfully blocks all 11 representative attacks across the four attack classes while introducing only 1.42 ms of additional median round-trip latency. Our results demonstrate that protocol- and mission-aware policy enforcement provides a practical approach for securing CSP-based spacecraft networks.

papers.title: VISTA: A Framework for Vision-Informed Semantic Traffic Awareness
papers.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming intelligent transportation systems by connecting roadside cameras, edge computing units, vehicles, and traffic infrastructure into a shared sensing and decision-making ecosystem. However, transmitting raw traffic video over vehicle-to-everything (V2X) links is bandwidth-intensive, while deploying large multimodal models directly on resource-constrained vehicles is often impractical. To address these limitations, this article proposes VISTA (Vision-Informed Semantic Traffic Awareness), a multimodal vision-language edge-intelligence framework that combines predictive video representation learning with lightweight language-based reasoning to provide communication-efficient traffic situational awareness. In the proposed architecture, roadside surveillance units employ the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA) and an attentive-pooler module to convert traffic video clips into compact future-scene embeddings. These embeddings are transmitted through V2X links to vehicle-mounted systems, where a TinyLlama small language model, enhanced with a custom visual adapter, interprets the embeddings alongside natural-language (NL) traffic queries. VISTA enables vehicles to obtain interpretable traffic information, reason about upcoming scene dynamics, and identify potential collision risks without receiving raw video streams. Experimental results in a digital-twin urban traffic environment show that VISTA achieves 97.77% accuracy and an 89% F1 score for future collision prediction while reducing the communication payload by several orders of magnitude compared with raw RGB video transmission. These results demonstrate the feasibility of embedding-based multimodal intelligence for low-latency, communication-efficient, and safety-oriented IoT-enabled transportation systems.

papers.title: Post-Quantum Migration of Wi-Fi Key Establishment: A Hybrid ML-KEM Design for OWE and FILS, Validated on OWE with hostapd
papers.abstract: The key agreements that protect a Wi-Fi connection rely on Diffie-Hellman, which a sufficiently capable quantum computer would break; an adversary can therefore record an association today and decrypt its traffic years later. Key establishment is thus the part of IEEE 802.11 that has to be migrated first. This work targets the two protocols that perform that agreement inside the frames used to set up the link: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption (OWE), which encrypts otherwise open networks, and Fast Initial Link Setup (FILS), designed for fast connection in dense and mobile deployments. We propose replacing their Diffie-Hellman exchange with a hybrid one that runs the classical elliptic-curve agreement alongside ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and derives the master key from both secrets, so the connection stays protected as long as either component remains unbroken. The exchange reuses the frames each protocol already sends and adds no extra round trip; an access point can advertise the hybrid mode alongside classical OWE, and a station configured to require it refuses to associate without a completed post-quantum exchange. Binding the advertised capabilities to the derived key is specified as a design extension and is not part of the prototype. We validate the design with a working implementation on hostapd and wpa_supplicant: both endpoints derive the same key in every measured connection, with the two smaller parameter sets each enlarged association frame fits in a single frame even under a conservative 1500-byte fragmentation threshold, and the added connection time and computation stay below half a millisecond. The measurements are obtained on OWE; the design carries over to FILS, whose frame budget is left for specific measurement. Of the three ML-KEM parameter sets, the intermediate one offers the best balance between security level and size.

papers.title: Network Intrusion Detection Adaptability under Spurious Labels: A Noise-Aware Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning Framework
papers.abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) must incrementally adapt to emerging attacks, even when only a limited amount of labeled network traffic is available. Consequently, Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL)-based NIDSs have gained growing attention. However, existing FSCIL-based NIDSs are highly vulnerable to label noise in newly-observed attack classes. To address this limitation, we propose NAFN, a noise-aware FSCIL-based NIDS framework that reduces the impact of mislabeled data during incremental adaptation. NAFN consists of two components: (i) Noise Detection, which identifies and removes mislabeled biflows using noise-detection algorithms, and (ii) Feature Sampling, which estimates class-conditional embeddings from clean biflows, calibrates them with base-class statistics, and resamples synthetic features to recover the original biflow count. The framework follows the Rethink Few-Shot (RFS) teacher-student paradigm with lightweight nearest-neighbor or logistic regression classifiers, and various pretraining & memory selection strategies. Experiments on CSE-CIC-IDS2018, Edge-IIoT, and IoT-NID datasets show that NAFN effectively preserves prior knowledge and maintains strong incremental performance even under 50% label noise, consistently improving new-class F1-scores over non-denoised baselines, up to +52%, while being time-efficient and robust in cross-network and high-noise incremental settings. The implementation is publicly available to foster reproducibility.

papers.title: A Survey on Cloud-Edge-Terminal Collaborative Intelligence in AIoT Networks
papers.abstract: The proliferation of Internet of things (IoT) devices in smart cities, transportation, healthcare, and industrial applications, coupled with the explosive growth of AI-driven services, has increased demands for efficient distributed computing architectures and networks, driving cloud-edge-terminal collaborative intelligence (CETCI) as a fundamental paradigm within the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) community. With advancements in deep learning, large language models (LLMs), and edge computing, CETCI has made significant progress with emerging AIoT applications, moving beyond isolated layer optimization to deployable collaborative intelligence systems for AIoT (CISAIOT), a practical research focus in AI, distributed computing, and communications. This survey describes foundational architectures, enabling technologies, and scenarios of CETCI paradigms, offering a tutorial-style review for CISAIOT beginners. We systematically analyze architectural components spanning cloud, edge, and terminal layers, examining core technologies including network virtualization, container orchestration, and software-defined networking, while presenting categorizations of collaboration paradigms that cover task offloading, resource allocation, and optimization across heterogeneous infrastructures. Furthermore, we explain intelligent collaboration learning frameworks by reviewing advances in federated learning, distributed deep learning, edge-cloud model evolution, and reinforcement learning-based methods. Finally, we discuss challenges (e.g., scalability, heterogeneity, interoperability) and future trends (e.g., 6G+, agents, quantum computing, digital twin), highlighting how integration of distributed computing and communication can address open issues and guide development of robust, efficient, and secure collaborative AIoT systems.

papers.title: A Layered Protocol Architecture for the Internet of Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can learn domain-specific languages such as APIs and tool interfaces, enabling agents that act through standardized protocols like MCP. But LLM context windows cannot grow indefinitely, so scaling beyond individual capacity requires agent collaboration: the "Internet of Agents" (IoA). Current network stacks (OSI, TCP/IP) were designed for data delivery, not semantic coordination, so we propose two new layers: an Agent Communication Layer (L8) that standardizes message envelopes, speech-act performatives, and interaction patterns; and an Agent Semantic Layer (L9) that negotiates a shared context, grounds and disambiguates content against it, and provides consensus primitives for population-scale coordination. On two real datasets and two LLMs, L9's schema-grounded disambiguation improves accuracy on ambiguous requests by 13--72 percentage points over blind guessing, at no added cost when disambiguation is not needed; an ablation shows this gain is schema-specific for open-domain QA but not for structured slot-filling, where the protocol's round-trip structure alone already suffices.

papers.title: DeGenTWeb: A First Look at MGT-dominant Websites
papers.abstract: Many news reports have claimed that machine-generated text (MGT) from large language models (LLMs) is taking over the web. However, these claims are typically not based on a representative sample of the web, and the methodology underlying them is often opaque. Consequently, we lack an understanding of the true prevalence and characteristics of MGT on the web. We describe DeGenTWeb, which systematically identifies MGT-dominant websites: sites whose informational prose content is mostly MGT, with little human input. We show how to adapt detectors of MGT for use on web pages, and how to aggregate detection results from multiple pages on a site for accurate site-level categorization. DeGenTWeb mislabels only 0.12% of human-authored sites as MGT-dominant. We find that 20.9% of the sites archived by Common Crawl between January and July 2026 and 13.6% of the sites linked from Bing's search results in 2025 are MGT-dominant. These figures are lower bounds on the prevalence of MGT-dominant sites. We also find that the fraction of MGT-dominant sites is growing over time, and that many such sites share the same owner. We will release all of our code and data after publication.

papers.title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Collaborative edge large language model (LLM) systems often require repeated prefill computation when task contexts are transferred between agents. Reusing previously computed key--value (KV) caches can eliminate this overhead, but requires KV-cache delivery before the receiving agent begins decoding. Under strict deadlines and unreliable edge links, complete KV cache transfer may be infeasible, making the timely delivery of useful KV information critical. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that combines prioritized source transmission with adaptive loss recovery. PriorityFEC first organizes KV blocks into a utility-aware source queue to prioritize important information. It then employs ACK-sliding Streaming FEC and a lightweight Double Deep Q-Network (Double-DQN) scheduler to dynamically balance source delivery and repair transmission under deadline constraints. We implement PriorityFEC in a distributed edge LLM-serving prototype and evaluate it using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across multiple workloads. Experimental results demonstrate that PriorityFEC preserves more useful KV information and achieves substantially higher task accuracy than competing transport schemes, particularly when the deadline is insufficient to deliver the complete KV cache.

papers.title: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity
papers.abstract: Satellite computations often outlast the paths and providers initially serving them. We argue that in-network computing should organize changing execution opportunities around one continuing logical computation: workers execute ready operations, while consumers recognize which results already contribute. We present an architecture separating logical computation, stream context, and physical binding, and show in wildfire assessment how retained observations support recomputation while reachable association history stays in place. A 300-node Linux prototype examines placement, dependency assembly, and continuation. Across 120 images, stage-wise placement delivers 82.08% of positions within deadlines versus 76.06% for single-node placement, while traces separate blocked output delivery from dependencies split across providers. Across 50 observations with 20-node isolation, Confirmation-Coordinated Rebinding (CCR) coordinates replanning, source replay, cross-attempt acceptance, and in-band confirmation to complete all 50 observations with verified outputs using seven replays and 13 ignored duplicate outputs.

papers.title: Cyber Resilience in Next-Generation Networks: Threat Landscape, Theoretical Foundations, and Design Paradigms
papers.abstract: The evolution of networked systems, driven by innovations in software-defined networking (SDN), network function virtualization (NFV), open radio access networks (O-RAN), and cloud-native architectures, is redefining both the operational landscape and the threat surface of critical infrastructures. This book offers an in-depth, interdisciplinary examination of how resilience must be re-conceptualized and re-engineered to address the multifaceted challenges posed by these transformations. Structured across six chapters, this book begins by surveying the contemporary risk landscape, identifying emerging cyber, physical, and AI-driven threats, and analyzing their implications for scalable, heterogeneous network environments. It then establishes rigorous definitions and evaluation frameworks for resilience, going beyond robustness and fault-tolerance to address adaptive, anticipatory, and retrospective mechanisms across diverse application domains. The core of the book delves into advanced paradigms and practical strategies for resilience, including zero trust architectures, game-theoretic threat modeling, and self-healing design principles. A significant portion is devoted to the role of artificial intelligence, especially reinforcement learning and large language models (LLMs), in enabling dynamic threat response, autonomous network control, and multi-agent coordination under uncertainty.

papers.title: RF-Based Macronutrient Estimation in Liquid Foods via Composition-Aware Multi-Task Learning
papers.abstract: Current approaches to macronutrient estimation range from high-overhead laboratory analysis to user-dependent methods such as manual nutritional lookup, reading package labels, and vision-based image analysis. These approaches are often time-consuming, input-dependent, or sensitive to imaging and measurement conditions. In this work, we investigate synchronous 2.4 GHz OFDM radio-frequency (RF) measurements for estimating carbohydrate, fat, and protein content in liquid foods. Using a controlled sensing setup, we study how liquid composition shapes frequency-domain RF responses -- a first step toward a sensor integrated into a liquid-contacting vessel that estimates macronutrient content passively and label-free, and toward composition-aware RF food analysis beyond liquids. We propose the Ingredient-Conditioned OFDM Transformer (ICOT), a structure-aware multi-task Transformer that operates on two-dimensional OFDM channel frequency response matrices. ICOT infers canonical ingredient categories representing dielectric-driver composition and uses them to condition macronutrient regression through feature concatenation. On 28,420 captures spanning 55 beverage classes, ICOT achieves an in-distribution MAE of 0.101 g/100 ml and an out-of-distribution MAE of 0.485 g/100 ml -- comparable in magnitude to deviations present in manufacturer-reported labels -- though generalization to novel formulations remains the primary open challenge.

papers.title: Budgeted Decision-Model-Guided Joint-Action Search for Satellite Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Efficient task offloading in satellite edge computing requires coordinated allocation of communication and computing resources. Search methods based on large language models (LLMs) have been shown to generate high-quality resource allocations, but the latency of individual model requests and repeated model interactions can lead to substantial solver overhead. We propose budgeted joint-action search (BJAS), an integrated decision-model-guided solver that jointly optimizes satellite offloading and power allocation to minimize average task-completion latency under explicit search budgets. Its bounded candidate pools combine single-terminal updates with power-inheriting offload replacements for batched selection, retaining two-terminal coordination without enumerating additional power vectors. Across 60 completed runs per method under the workflows' respective configurations, BJAS reduces mean total solver time by 97.16% relative to LLM-generated offloading while achieving a mean task-completion latency close to that of the LLM baseline. BJAS also achieves lower mean task-completion latency than the tested genetic algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient baselines.

papers.title: Feedback-Aware Residual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Timely Communication in Cognitive Radio Networks
papers.abstract: Supporting time-sensitive services in cognitive radio networks requires distributed access strategies that translate shared spectrum opportunities into timely packet delivery. Achieving this objective is challenging because reception conditions are only partially observable to individual transmitters, while dynamic competition and access overhead constrain the service that can be completed within packet deadlines. We formulate a distributed access problem that captures the coupling among interference-dependent reception, queue evolution, and protocol durations. To address this problem, we propose feedback-aware residual multi-agent proximal policy optimization (FAR-MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution. The method constructs channel-specific historical feedback representations that complement instantaneous sensing with evidence from completed access attempts. A residual policy network integrates this experience with current observations and packet urgency to guide local access decisions. Numerical results show improved timely delivery over the baseline methods, particularly under heavy traffic and bursty arrivals with mixed packet deadlines.

papers.title: EdgeNet City: Context-Aware AI-RAN Planning toward Autonomous Urban Connectivity
papers.abstract: The evolution from 5G toward 6G calls for more anticipatory and context-aware Cell-on-Wheels (COW) planning in wireless networks. We present EdgeNet City, an online framework that grounds free-form natural-language inputs in geographic activity representations and path-gain data. A catalog-referenced representation links activity roles, geographic features and predefined demand profiles, separating semantic selection from deterministic spatial computation. The algorithm combines prescribed demand with relative propagation support to screen service areas for subsequent COW assessment. We publicly release a London dataset with 22,678 transmitters, approximately 449.4 billion path-gain records and retained receiver geometry. Within prepared propagation domains, the online prototype reuses these records without new ray tracing or live operator measurements. In a matched 20-event study across six London environments, the expanded representation increases mean spatial overlap with the reused full technical-review reference from 0.4929 for the single-feature Venue-only baseline to 0.7203. Rule-based and language-model planners select identical activities in this panel. With need-aware ranking and a three-cell diagnostic budget fixed, the expanded representation increases mean Reference-need Capture by 25.44 percentage points over Venue-only.

papers.title: SliceWise: Traffic-Aware Multi-Agent RL with Temporal Encoding for Joint Slice Admission and Resource Orchestration in O-RAN
papers.abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) services in mission-critical applications such as industrial automation, remote healthcare, and autonomous systems demand stringent quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees under dynamic, resource-constrained wireless conditions. Open radio access networks (O-RAN) offer a software-defined and programmable foundation for embedding AI-driven control. This letter proposes SliceWise, a traffic-aware multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for joint admission control, user-slice association, and resource orchestration in O-RAN. The control problem is modeled as a cooperative multi-agent Markov decision process, with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks capturing temporal traffic dynamics and dueling double deep Q-networks (D3QN) ensuring stable learning. Simulation results show that SliceWise substantially reduces delay violations and packet drops while improving slice-level reliability and resource efficiency, offering a scalable orchestration solution for AI-native O-RAN deployments.

papers.title: Diagnosis as Percolation on an Evidence Graph: Root-Cause Recoverability in Network Fault Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Diagnosing failures from incomplete observations presents three challenges: determining whether sufficient evidence connects a possible cause to a symptom, distinguishing the true cause from plausible alternatives, and assessing when a diagnosis can be trusted. We introduce an evidence-graph framework that separates these challenges and uses percolation theory to analyze how missing information affects cause-symptom connectivity. In controlled simulations with an average degree of four, a giant connected component emerges when approximately 25% of evidence is retained, but a specific cause-alarm pair reaches 50% connectivity only after slightly more than half is retained. Even connectivity does not guarantee correct cause identification. We apply this framework to multi-LLM diagnosis of IEEE 802.11 packet captures. A final reconciliation pass improves evidence-grounding weighted F1 from 0.912 to 0.964, primarily by removing isolated citations rather than connecting previously separate evidence chains, consistently across three graph constructions. However, connectivity is not a reliable confidence measure: its association with diagnostic quality becomes statistically insignificant after controlling for capture length, citation count, within-capture dependence, and multiple comparisons. Further experiments show that directed and weighted edges help selectively, while simpler overlap measures or domain-specific methods sometimes perform better. These findings establish evidence graphs as a framework for separating evidence availability, causal distinguishability, and confidence reliability, while demonstrating that connected evidence alone cannot certify diagnostic correctness.

papers.title: IZM-DSR: A New Zone-Disjoint Multi-path Routing Algorithm for Mobile Ad-Hoc Network
papers.abstract: Some of multi-path routing algorithms in MANETs use multiple paths simultaneously. These algorithms can attempt to find node-disjoint to achieve higher fault tolerance. By using node-disjoint paths, it is expected that the end-to-end delay in each case should be independent of each other. However, because of natural properties and medium access mechanisms in ad hoc networks, such as CSMA/CA, the endto-end delay between any source and destination depends on the pattern of communication in the neighborhood region. In this case some of the intermediate nodes should be silent to reverence their neighbors and this matter increases the end-toend delay. To avoid this problem, multi-path routing algorithms can use zone-disjoint paths instead of node-disjoint paths. In this paper we propose a new multi-path routing algorithm that selects zone-disjoint paths, using omnidirectional antenna. We evaluate our algorithm in several different scenarios. The simulation results show that our approach is very effective in decreasing routing overhead and end-to-end delay.

papers.title: Design Rules for Low-Latency Multipath Congestion Control
papers.abstract: We first study optimal congestion control from a theoretical perspective. Concretely, we consider a system that optimizes the sum of the utilities of all the users, in which the users are allowed to send their traffic over different paths over the network and derive design rules that optimal (low-latency) multipath congestion control needs to follow. Because, as it turns out that optimal congestion control requires coordination between the network nodes, and hence, is hard to implement, we investigate how to approximate its performance with algorithms in which (i) the network nodes make independent decisions and (ii) coordination is only allowed between the subflows that belong to the same user. Therefore, these design rules need to be slightly relaxed. We compare the performance of these realistic algorithms with the optimal algorithm. We also investigate to what extent the algorithms that are currently defined and are being defined in the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), in particular, (i) Prague congestion control (i.e., congestion control based on Accurate Explicit Congestion Notification (AccECN) marks) and (ii) a variant of a loss-based multipath congestion control algorithm, adhere to these rules.

papers.title: Prediction-Driven Contract Matching with Controlled Overbooking for Cloud-Edge DDoS Scrubbing Markets
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) scrubbing requires ex-ante capacity commitments under uncertain traffic, heterogeneous budgets, resource costs, and fulfillment risks. We develop a prediction-driven two-stage contracting mechanism coordinating business entities (BEs), edge scrubbing nodes (ESs), and a cloud scrubbing center (CS) through BE-ES (B&E) main-service and ES-CS (E&C) supplementary contracts. In the first offline phase, Transformer forecasts generate candidate reserved scrubbing rates, generalized Nash bargaining determines candidate prices, and interim many-to-one B&E matching permits controlled overbooking under scenario-based aggregate ES shortfall-risk assessment. In the second offline phase, formal E&C reservations are established subject to capacity and payment constraints; their finalized rates and prices update ES-side proxy scores and guide localized risk-aware B&E contract adjustment. During online fulfillment, an edge-first, cloud-assisted weighted proportional allocation policy allocates scrubbing capacity under finalized contracts without rematching, renegotiation, or additional cloud reservations. Experiments with CICDDoS2019-derived workloads show that the proposed mechanism satisfies the prescribed empirical shortfall-risk criterion across all 100 evaluated horizon-instance pairs, whereas the NoRisk ablation violates it in all 100. Runtime measurements indicate lightweight online fulfillment relative to offline contract formation. The evaluated configurations also exhibit limited overall scrubbing coverage and near-zero realized cloud utilization.

papers.title: Early UAV Detection Using 5G NR LEO Downlinks for Passive ISAC
papers.abstract: 5G New Radio (NR) low-Earth-orbit (LEO) downlinks enable passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection. Weak echoes require motion-compensated accumulation, but exhaustive searches postpone alerts. We propose a receiver that combines selective Doppler-rate search, early UAV alerts and continued delay-Doppler estimation. Classical, statistical and neural configurations select rates of Doppler change to search, while a shared correlation score determines detection. Simulated echo delay, Doppler and power follow the moving satellite-UAV-receiver geometry, propagation loss, assumed scattering and antenna response. In a line-of-sight scene with acquired beams and UAVs at 5-8 km horizontal distance, all three configurations match exhaustive search at 92.9% correct final detections, with 0.10-0.13% observed false alerts on no-UAV recordings. The neural configuration reduces mean time to the first correct alert by 36.5% versus exhaustive search and 21.9% versus the closest literature baseline, averaging over successfully detected UAVs. These results demonstrate earlier UAV alerts while preserving exhaustive search's final detection accuracy, supporting passive sensing over cellular satellites.

papers.title: Disaggregated LLM Inference in Space: A Communication Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: Orbital data centers could enable large-scale AI inference, but efficiently serving a frontier language model to many users may require several compute satellites to cooperate over optical links. While disaggregated inference, which splits large language model (LLM) serving across machines, is well established in terrestrial data centers, its viability under the unique constraints of orbital deployments remains an open question. This article investigates how link capacity and satellite separation affect two types of disaggregated LLM serving, in both compact satellite formations and distributed constellations. Prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) migrates a large KV cache once per request, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) exchanges small activations at every mixture-of-experts layer for every generated token. The two respond to distance in different ways. PDD is limited mainly by link capacity and, with fast enough links, tolerates separations of up to a thousand kilometers. AFD is limited mainly by propagation delay, which accumulates layer by layer and forces attention and expert instances within about a kilometer of each other. Based on these results, we propose a hierarchical orbital inference architecture and provide network design guidelines for future orbital data centers, including the role of ground access latency.

papers.title: Adaptive Wake-on-Radio Communication for Batteryless IoT Systems
papers.abstract: Batteryless Internet of Things (IoT) systems powered by energy harvesting require communication mechanisms that dynamically adapt to fluctuating energy availability while maintaining ultra-low-power operation. This paper presents a Wake-on-Radio (WoR) communication framework for low-power intermittent IoT systems in which the node's communication state adapts to its stored energy. The framework uses a batteryless IoT node that integrates a photovoltaic harvester, a 570 $\mu$F capacitor, two voltage supervisors, and a microcontroller. The voltage supervisors drive an energy-aware finite state machine that switches the node between Shutdown, Low-Power Listening (LPL), Transmit, and Receive modes. The proposed system employs the integrated WoR capability of the transceiver, eliminating the need for additional wake-up hardware. For the evaluated traffic conditions and an LPL wake-up rate of 16 Hz, the measured power consumption is approximately 1.2 $\mu$W in the Shutdown mode, 300 $\mu$W during LPL, 531 $\mu$W for reception, and 627 $\mu$W for transmission. System-level experiments under solar-harvesting operation validate the proposed framework, demonstrating reliable bidirectional communication with no packet losses observed across repeated runs at a harvested input power of 1.2 mW.

papers.title: An Alternative to Crawlers: Scalable P2P Network Monitoring Using the Network Scale-Up Method
papers.abstract: \Ac{p2p} networks have remained an active area of research and development for decades. Originally used for data dissemination, they have later become instrumental to decentralized payment systems, blockchains, and Web3 applications. Since decentralization is a crucial property of these networks, they are continuously monitored to track attributes such as the geographical distribution of nodes, which serve as indicators of infrastructure concentration and resilience. However, monitoring typically relies on network crawls to derive accurate snapshots, which requires substantial computational and network resources. In contrast, \ac{nsum} is a statistical tool that estimates the prevalence of subpopulations based on responses to questions such as \enquote{How many people do you know in a specific group?} This work leverages the information embedded in Kademlia routing tables to develop a lightweight \ac{nsum}-based measurement and estimation framework that infers global network attribute distributions from a small set of nodes, offering an alternative to full-network crawls. As a case study, we evaluate our approach on \ac{ipfs}, a well-researched and widely used Web3 data storage and retrieval network. This is the first application of \ac{nsum} to decentralized network measurement. We evaluate our methodology on two datasets: the first comprises 360 full-network crawls collected over one month to assess our measurement-estimation approach across multiple simulated measurement scenarios, while the second dataset was collected through a deployment of the proposed lightweight measurement framework during May 2026. The results show that local Kademlia routing views, with only 10 nodes, preserve sufficient information to accurately estimate global attribute distributions, achieving normalized biases below \SI{10}{\percent} and closely tracking temporal changes in network composition.

papers.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
papers.abstract: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability $q$, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints $f_s$ and $f_r$, respectively. The sampler-transmitter pair jointly decides whether to idle, retransmit a stale packet, or replace it with a fresh sample. We derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information, analyze a class of stationary randomized policies, and obtain an optimal policy within this class that provides a $4$-approximation guarantee. The joint problem reduces to the sampling-constrained problem when $f_s\leq qf_r$ and the transmission-constrained problem when $f_s\geq f_r$. For $qf_r<f_s<f_r$, we formulate a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and introduce the class $\bar{\Pi}$ of $(W,R)$ policies, where $W$ specifies a waiting threshold for transmission and $R$ specifies a packet-replacement threshold. We prove that, for every choice of Lagrange multipliers, the corresponding Lagrangian-relaxed Markov decision process admits an optimal policy in $\bar{\Pi}$. We then formulate a linear program (LP) over distributions of $(W,R)$ policies and prove that choosing a policy according to an optimal LP solution yields an optimal CMDP policy. Moreover, there exists an optimal LP solution assigning positive probability to at most three $(W,R)$ policies. Since $\bar{\Pi}$ is countably infinite, for every $\epsilon>0$ we construct a finite subset $\bar{\Pi}_{\epsilon}\subset\bar{\Pi}$ and show that the LP restricted to this set yields an $\epsilon$-optimal policy. Finally, we derive a stronger pair of lower bounds by considering systems with only the sampling-rate or transmission-rate constraint. Using these bounds, we construct a policy randomizing among four $(W,R)$ policies with a $2$-approximation guarantee for $qf_r<f_s<f_r$.

papers.title: Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. In this paper, we address the efficient collaborative inference under a realistic communication scenario. We propose a wireless edge-assisted framework for adaptive latent reasoning (WEALR) that augments onboard computation with edge computing. A decision-making agent jointly selects the execution location and latent-reasoning convergence threshold. We formulate this joint adaptation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A Lagrangian-constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) approach, namely trust region policy optimization Lagrangian (TRPO-Lag), learns to balance task performance and resource consumption under varying wireless conditions and task requirements. We evaluate the framework using LIBERO manipulation tasks, profiled VLA inference costs, and ray-traced wireless channels. Experimental results demonstrate that TRPO-Lag achieves up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success rate compared to benchmark CDRL methods.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Techniques for Distributed Entanglement Generation and Purification
papers.abstract: We develop a purification-aware optimization framework for distributing high-fidelity entangled states over quantum networks. In repeater-based architectures, the framework jointly selects entanglement swapping, fusion or graph-state growth, and purification operations to maximize generation rate under a fidelity threshold. Different purification models can be incorporated through their fidelity-update, success-probability, and latency rules. We introduce purification-augmented generation trees and dynamic programming (DP) algorithms for entangled-pair (EP) distribution. Hypergraph-flow linear programming (LP) formulations support level-based structures and concurrent generation across multiple trees and demands. We extend the framework to GHZ states and arbitrary graph states constructed from remote EP resources, introduce graph-state construction primitives, and derive closed-form fidelity-vector updates for GHZ fusion and purification and graph-state growth and purification. We provide optimal formulations under the adopted models, discretization, and purification bounds, together with efficient DP and LP heuristics. We bound fidelity- and rate-discretization errors and establish convergence for fixed constructions under stated regularity conditions. NetSquid simulations of EP generation using our LP approach show an average 160% increase in generation rate over the compared prior approaches, with gains up to 330% in some scenarios. GHZ and graph-state simulations demonstrate the heuristics' effectiveness in balancing generation rate, output fidelity, and computational overhead.

papers.title: HELENA for 5G NR LEO NTN Channel Estimation: A Comparative Evaluation
papers.abstract: Deep Learning (DL)-based channel estimation has shown high accuracy and low latency in terrestrial 5G NR, but Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) introduce Doppler and synchronization impairments that may require NTN-specific architectures. We investigate whether HELENA, a dual-attention neural channel estimator originally designed for terrestrial channels, remains effective after NTN retraining and suitable across high-performance and power-constrained inference platforms. Its unchanged architecture is trained on paired receiver-compensated and residual-impaired datasets and evaluated alongside terrestrial-origin, NTN-specific, and classical estimators. HELENA's SNR-averaged Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE), computed by arithmetic averaging in linear scale, remains within 0.29 and 0.72 dB of the most accurate learned estimator, AttRNet, in the two conditions, respectively. It outperforms global Linear Minimum Mean Squared Error (LMMSE) under compensation and all evaluated LMMSE variants under residual impairments, although profile-aware filtering achieves lower error under compensation. On an RTX PRO 4500, FP16 TensorRT inference reaches 0.0573 ms 99th-Percentile (P99) latency, below the adopted 0.5 ms estimator budget. On a 10 W Jetson Orin NX, HELENA consumes 66.0% less energy per sample than AttRNet, but its 0.9620 ms P99 exceeds the budget; only the less accurate LSiDNN-48 meets it. Thus, HELENA remains effective without NTN-specific redesign for the evaluated task, while accurate embedded inference remains a latency challenge.

papers.title: Mind the Gap: Cross-RFC Formal Analysis Exposes DNSSEC's Hidden Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: This paper presents a cross-RFC formal analysis of selected DNSSEC mechanisms using SAPIC+ models of cryptographic operations and stateful caching. We analyze properties concerning data origin authenticity, integrity, chain of trust, and authenticated denial of existence within these models. Our analysis shows that core authentication properties hold under the modeled assumptions, while wildcard expansion, the mechanism that bridges positive and negative authentication, exhibits a cross-RFC interaction vulnerability that defeats DNSSEC's integrity guarantee. Specifically, we discover Cross-Zone Wildcard Cache Poisoning: a new attack in which a malicious zone operator exploits a gap in the DNSSEC specifications to poison resolver caches with forged records for some domains outside its authority, served to clients as DNSSEC-authentic. The tested versions of all four major resolvers implementing the affected caching optimization accept the malformed wildcard material. The resulting impact depends on the resolver's synthesis path. All four vendors have publicly released fixes. The distinctive integrity failure is a synthesized, attacker-chosen positive answer with the Authenticated Data (AD) bit set: prior attacks instead exhausted availability, downgraded to AD=0, or skipped validation. Our models also identify two cross-RFC availability flaws and rediscover three known attack classes. We test six resolvers and measure deployment prerequisites through focused resolver and TLD scans. We propose updates to four RFCs.

papers.title: Securing SIM-Assisted Wireless Networks via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) have recently emerged as a powerful wave-domain technology that enables multi-stage manipulation of electromagnetic signals through multilayer programmable architectures. While SIMs offer unprecedented degrees of freedom for enhancing physical-layer security, their extremely large number of meta-atoms leads to a high-dimensional and strongly coupled optimization space, making conventional design approaches inefficient and difficult to scale. Moreover, existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques suffer from slow convergence and performance degradation in dynamic wireless environments with imperfect knowledge of passive eavesdroppers. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid quantum proximal policy optimization (QPPO) framework for SIM-assisted secure communications that jointly optimizes transmit power allocation and SIM phase shifts to maximize the average secrecy rate under power and quality-of-service constraints. Specifically, a parameterized quantum circuit is embedded into the actor network, forming a hybrid classical-quantum policy architecture that enhances policy representation capability and exploration efficiency in high-dimensional continuous action spaces. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed Q-PPO scheme consistently outperforms DRL baselines, achieving approximately 15% higher secrecy rates and 30% faster convergence under imperfect eavesdropper channel state information. These results establish Q-PPO as a powerful optimization paradigm for SIM-enabled secure wireless networks.

papers.title: LZn : Robust LoRa Frame Synchronization Under Frame Collisions and Ultra-Low SNR Conditions
papers.abstract: LoRa has become a widely adopted wireless modulation scheme in LPWANs due to its low cost, long range, and minimal transmission power. However, collisions between frames of the same spreading factor -- common in dense LoRa deployments -- prevent conventional LoRa receivers from detecting and correctly decoding frames. Recent work has introduced methods to improve recovery, yet their detection stage degrades sharply under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and high collision rates. In this work, we introduce LZn, a synchronization scheme driven by a minimum-based spectral intersection across consecutive symbols. While preamble search incurs a modest overhead, LZn reduces the cost of fine synchronization by two to three orders of magnitude compared to existing collision-tolerant receivers. Our method enables robust frame synchronization even under multiple packet overlaps or extremely low SNR conditions. We evaluate LZn on simulations and three independent, real-world LoRa datasets. LZn improves detection sensitivity by up to 10 dB and increases detection probability by up to 1.54x. In real-world datasets, LZn improves decoding by 3.46x in the most challenging single-user scenario and up to 1.22x in collision scenarios compared to the second best collision-tolerant scheme (TnB). These results demonstrate that LZn substantially improves the frame recovery of LoRa receivers, while remaining compatible with real-time requirements.
